runs.text: View: Ares Capital Corporation's December 31, 2024 evaluated debt disclosures support a bounded historical market-implied-risk analysis, not an executable market view. The July 2029 note's evaluated equivalent of 101.294118 per100 implies conditional maturity yields of 5.622366% in case A (equivalent treated as clean) and 6.316949% in case B (treated as dirty). Neither price-basis assumption wins on the evidence. Against a simple same-date Treasury comparison of 4.354685%, the respective spreads are 126.768113 and 196.226407 basis points. Those spreads compensate for a mixture of credit, liquidity, optionality, conventions and unexplained factors; they do not identify factual default probabilities. Positive published statutory coverage supports a funding-flexibility countercase, but cannot certify drawable liquidity or show that the market adequately compensates unsecured creditors.

The strongest supported market signal is a positive but convention-sensitive July 2029 yield premium to Treasury, not a distress verdict or a security preference. A291's 861 USDm Level 2 fair value divided by 850 USDm principal produces an evaluated equivalent, not an observed executable clean price. Unknown basis alone moves the maturity yield by about 69.458294bp between A and B—far more than the roughly 1.5bp rounding sensitivity within each case. Under A the June 15, 2029 par-call leg has the lower yield; under B maturity does. That reversal makes it especially important not to silently declare a unique contractual yield-to-worst. Source fair values improved versus 2023 for the eight continuing series, but those point changes exclude coupons, reinvestment and trading costs and are not total returns. The low 86 equivalent for the 3.200% November 2031 series cannot establish relative credit weakness versus a 7.000% January 2027 series above par.

Evidence → mechanism → creditor consequence: A94's swaps align issuer funding with a primarily floating-rate loan portfolio; this is BDC matched funding, not industrial EBITDA leverage. A95's unsecured payment ranking gives equal payment status against non-subordinated unsecured debt, but collateral priority and subsidiary claims reduce direct asset access separately. C4's published 196.2% statutory coverage against 150% supports historical financing flexibility; a fall in portfolio values would reduce the coverage numerator, potentially tighten borrowing-base eligibility and funding access, and make refinancing maturing parent debt more dependent on asset repayments/sales or equity. Added secured borrowing could preserve cash while reducing unsecured access to pledged value. No numerical recovery or probability follows from those mechanisms.

The strongest supported countercase is the positive historical 46.2 percentage-point published coverage margin, the issuer's dated material-compliance assertions, conditional funding access, and subsequent January 2025 capital-market issuance (A95; C4 T4C.4, T4C.5). It would win against an immediate funding-closure thesis if dated certificates demonstrated adequate pro forma coverage, borrowing-base eligibility, equity tests, lender commitments and accessible cash after intended uses. Those conditions are not supplied, so this countercase reduces conviction in distress inference without proving value or implementation readiness. The initiating deterioration to monitor is weaker loan performance/marks; the first financial break would be lost asset backing or funding eligibility, followed by restricted liquidity and more expensive or constrained refinancing. Observable tests are coverage disclosures, facility certificates, portfolio marks, actual draws and shareholder-return execution—not an unsupported generic recession shock.

fields.value: View: Ares Capital Corporation's December 31, 2024 evaluated debt disclosures support a bounded historical market-implied-risk analysis, not an executable market view. The July 2029 note's evaluated equivalent of 101.294118 per100 implies conditional maturity yields of 5.622366% in case A (equivalent treated as clean) and 6.316949% in case B (treated as dirty). Neither price-basis assumption wins on the evidence. Against a simple same-date Treasury comparison of 4.354685%, the respective spreads are 126.768113 and 196.226407 basis points. Those spreads compensate for a mixture of credit, liquidity, optionality, conventions and unexplained factors; they do not identify factual default probabilities. Positive published statutory coverage supports a funding-flexibility countercase, but cannot certify drawable liquidity or show that the market adequately compensates unsecured creditors.

fields.value: The strongest supported market signal is a **positive but convention-sensitive July 2029 yield premium to Treasury**, not a distress verdict or a security preference. A291's 861 USDm Level 2 fair value divided by 850 USDm principal produces an evaluated equivalent, not an observed executable clean price. Unknown basis alone moves the maturity yield by about 69.458294bp between A and B—far more than the roughly 1.5bp rounding sensitivity within each case. Under A the June 15, 2029 par-call leg has the lower yield; under B maturity does. That reversal makes it especially important not to silently declare a unique contractual yield-to-worst. Source fair values improved versus 2023 for the eight continuing series, but those point changes exclude coupons, reinvestment and trading costs and are not total returns. The low 86 equivalent for the 3.200% November 2031 series cannot establish relative credit weakness versus a 7.000% January 2027 series above par.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence → mechanism → creditor consequence: A94's swaps align issuer funding with a primarily floating-rate loan portfolio; this is BDC matched funding, not industrial EBITDA leverage. A95's unsecured payment ranking gives equal payment status against non-subordinated unsecured debt, but collateral priority and subsidiary claims reduce direct asset access separately. C4's published 196.2% statutory coverage against 150% supports historical financing flexibility; a fall in portfolio values would reduce the coverage numerator, potentially tighten borrowing-base eligibility and funding access, and make refinancing maturing parent debt more dependent on asset repayments/sales or equity. Added secured borrowing could preserve cash while reducing unsecured access to pledged value. No numerical recovery or probability follows from those mechanisms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest supported countercase is the positive historical 46.2 percentage-point published coverage margin, the issuer's dated material-compliance assertions, conditional funding access, and subsequent January 2025 capital-market issuance (A95; C4 T4C.4, T4C.5). It would win against an immediate funding-closure thesis if dated certificates demonstrated adequate pro forma coverage, borrowing-base eligibility, equity tests, lender commitments and accessible cash after intended uses. Those conditions are not supplied, so this countercase reduces conviction in distress inference without proving value or implementation readiness. The initiating deterioration to monitor is weaker loan performance/marks; the first financial break would be lost asset backing or funding eligibility, followed by restricted liquidity and more expensive or constrained refinancing. Observable tests are coverage disclosures, facility certificates, portfolio marks, actual draws and shareholder-return execution—not an unsupported generic recession shock.
